Send security packet (SOC2, ISO, SSO/KMS notes) and partner NDA link by 2026-03-13
Share draft co-sell revenue split and ops RACI for review by 2026-03-19
action_items: Sophie Martinez: Send partner intro deck and co-sell one-pager (due 2026-03-13)
Daniel Ng: Prepare lightweight benchmark harness + sample payloads (due 2026-03-17)

summary: Intro call to scope a co-sell pilot between Redwood and Bridgewater focused on joint GTM for analytics augmentation. Main topics: partner roles, technical constraints (VPC, data residency, KMS), latency/cost targets, and next steps for a benchmark and security review.
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-03-11, Start: 15:00 PDT, Duration: ~48 minutes. Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM), Ethan (Bridgewater Partnerships), Maya (GT M), Liam (Solutions Architect).

Summary: Quick intros, each side's goals, then deep dive on ops and technical gating items. Agreed to run an initial benchmark and exchange security docs.

00:00 Sophie Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intros from our side: I'm Sophie, I'm the AE, Daniel here is our SE, Priya's our CSM.

00:22 Ethan Cole: Thanks Sophie, appreciate it. I'm Ethan, lead partnerships at Bridgewater, with Maya and Liam. We run a network of analytics integrations and we're exploring co-sell motion for an LLM-augmented insights feature.

00:40 Sophie Martinez: Great. High level — we want to make sure we understand your go-to-market and the ops questions up front. Daniel, do you want to give a 90-second on Redwood's co-sell capabilities?

00:55 Daniel Ng: Yep. Redwood's infra runs hosted, dedicated and private deployments, so for partners we usually align on either a hosted joint flow or a dedicated instance per strategic account. We do KV caching, continuous batching, fallback routing, uh — some teams call out our comp... uh, kernel selection optimizations.

01:18 Maya Rivera: Quick clarifying Q: when you say dedicated, is that like a reserved GPU pool we control, or you manage it and we get SLA?

01:28 Daniel Ng: It's a reserved capacity model — Redwood Dedicated — sorry, sometimes I say 'Red wood Dedecate' when I'm on calls, but it's reserved GPU capacity with an SLA and an option for network peering or VPC. You can pin model versions and we support KMS for keys.

01:45 Ethan Cole: Helpful. Our initial ask is twofold: one, we need a predictable latency envelope — sub 150ms p99 for short prompts for our frontline analytics assistant; two, we need a clean co-sell ops workflow — who owns provisioning, billing, and support.

02:03 Priya Patel: On ops we usually propose a triage: Redwood handles infra, we provide an onboarding runbook and a joint success plan. For billing, there are a couple of models — partner-resold versus referral revenue split. We'll draft a RACI after we see deal volume.

02:22 Liam O'Neill: On the technical side, a couple constraints: our customers require data residency in EU for a subset, and some enterprise accounts require SAML SSO and audit logs forwarded to their SIEM. Also we run some prompts that use large tabular payloads so tokenization costs matter.

02:46 Daniel Ng: Okay. For data residency we can route to region-specific infra or do a private deployment. SSO is supported — we integrate with SAML and SSO providers and have audit logging. For large tabular payloads we'd recommend prefix caching and possibly quantization on model variants — tradeoff is slight quality variance.

03:10 Maya Rivera: Important to flag — we also have strict procurement windows. If you want to co-sell into our top 10 accounts in Q2, we'll need pricing and legal redlines by mid-April.

03:21 Sophie Martinez: Understood. We'll prioritize the price deck if this goes toward a pilot. We'll also share our standard partner SOW template.

03:32 Ethan Cole: Curious about benchmarking — how do you usually run perf tests with partners? We have internal latency targets and also want to measure cost per active query.

03:43 Daniel Ng: We run a lightweight harness. Best practice: you give us a representative prompt set (anonymized), sample concurrency profile and target region. We'll run a runbook that measures p50/p95/p99 and token cost. We can simulate real traffic patterns. We'll put results into a spreadsheet and annotate recommended deployment (hosted vs dedicated vs private).

04:10 Liam O'Neill: We'll need guarantees on KV cache correctness — some of our prompts depend on prefix state. Does Redwood preserve per-session KV with dedicated deployments?

04:23 Daniel Ng: Yes, KV cache is session-based and persistent for the session life; worst case fallback is that we drop to a compatible stateless model variant — there was that one note about KV eviction policies with very long tails, but we can tune cache size and TTL in dedicated setups.

04:45 Maya Rivera: Security — can you send SOC2 report and encryption details? Also how does Redwood isolate customer data in hosted mode?

04:54 Sophie Martinez: Absolutely. We'll share our security packet: SOC2, ISO summary, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integration notes, and our incident response playbook. For hosted mode we logical-tenant isolate and strict access controls; for additional isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private with VPC peering. We'll post the packet and the NDA link after the call.

05:12 Ethan Cole: Perfect. A few partnership-level questions: revenue split expectations, co-marketing commitments, and lead routing. We also want to know how the support handoff looks.

05:26 Priya Patel: For support, standard approach: first-line support via Bridgewater, escalation to Redwood SE triage. For pilot accounts Redwood can provide a designated SE and 24-48 hour SLA for priority issues. Revenue split we'll add into the draft; typically it depends on who invoices and support burden.

05:48 Sophie Martinez: Quick note — we've seen the main objections are latency vs cost. There's often a hybrid play where you run a smaller, lower-latency model on dedicated infra for low-latency queries and route heavier reasoning to larger hosted models. That reduces cost while hitting p99 targets.

06:09 Liam O'Neill: Hmm. That hybrid routing could work. We also want to avoid double-billing customers. If Bridgewater resells, how is Metering surfaced?

06:21 Daniel Ng: Metering can be surfaced via APIs and per-route dashboards. We provide token-level breakdowns, per-route latency and cost. We can also export usage to a partner-facing billing CSV.

06:38 Ethan Cole: Can we pilot with three accounts? One EU-regulated, one NA enterprise, one mid-market — to get a spread.

06:46 Sophie Martinez: Yes, that seems reasonable. Action: Liam to share anonymized prompt set and list of pilot accounts. Daniel will run bench. Sophie will send deck and security. Priya will draft ops RACI.

07:02 Maya Rivera: Any blockers on our legal side? We have standard terms but we'll need a data processing addendum for EU accounts.

07:12 Sophie Martinez: We have a DPA template; we'll include it with the security packet. If they need on-prem or private deployments we can also provide a separate agreement.

07:24 Ethan Cole: Competitor question — we've been looking at AtlasAI and VectorCloud; what is the differentiator?

07:33 Daniel Ng: Quick differentiation: we focus on production-grade inference controls — routing, autoscaling, prefix caching and first-class observability. We also provide a single developer experience across hosted/dedicated/private which simplifies co-sell ops. Plus we have explicit tooling for batching/quantization recommendations to reduce unit cost.

07:58 Maya Rivera: Sounds good. One last logistics Q — do you have a partner referral/credit model for early pilots?

08:06 Sophie Martinez: We do — we can offer pilot credits and reduced pricing for the first 90 days for co-sell pilots. We'll put numbers in the pricing sheet.

08:16 Liam O'Neill: Excellent.

08:20 Sophie Martinez: Ok let's recap the next steps — Sophie to send partner intro deck, security packet and NDA link by Friday 2026-03-13; Daniel to prep the benchmark harness and example payloads by 2026-03-17; Liam to share anonymized prompt set and pilot account list by 2026-03-15; Priya to create a draft ops RACI and escalation matrix by 2026-03-19. We will tentatively schedule the benchmark run for week of 2026-03-22.

08:57 Ethan Cole: Thanks — that timeline works. We'll review and flag any procurement timing conflicts.

09:04 Sophie Martinez: Great. Thanks all. We'll follow up in email with links: partner deck (https://redwood.example/sales/deck/bridgewater-intro), benchmark spreadsheet placeholder (https://redwood.example/sales/benchmarks/bridgewater-run), and security packet (link to shared drive).

09:28 Maya Rivera: Thanks everyone.

09:31 Call ends — notes: transcription automated, some proper nouns may be off (Redwood Dedicated sometimes transcribed odd), occasional words merged.

References to shared artifacts: partner intro deck link above; benchmark spreadsheet; security packet (SOC2, DPA).
